key_insight: Most surveyed patients and carers supported AI-assisted duodenal biopsy diagnosis, while stakeholders emphasized accuracy, human oversight and transparency.
clinical_relevance: AI could help address pathology workload and diagnostic delays, but healthcare professionals preferred an assistant model over full automation.
method: Mixed-methods engagement using questionnaires, workshops and thematic analysis.
Patient and carer survey: 231 respondents; healthcare professional survey: 37 respondents.
Pre/post educational-session attitudes assessed in 34 matched participants.
evidence_signal: Patient and carer support was 68.4%; in the 34-person paired assessment, trust increased from 38.2% to 67.6% after education, but diagnostic performance was not evaluated.
watch_item: Stakeholder acceptance does not establish clinical safety or accuracy; deployment requires validation, governance and clear human oversight.
paper_title: Patient, carer and clinical stakeholder views on using artificial intelligence and machine learning for the histopathological diagnosis of duodenal biopsies
